text:
`python3 -m unittest` now passes all 25 tests. I fixed six defects, and I didn't modify the tests.

- **`queue.py`:** `_Entry.sort_key` returned `(seq, -priority)`. It now returns `(-priority, seq)`, so higher priority goes first and ties go in FIFO order.
- **`retry.py`:** `should_retry` used `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1`, which gave up one attempt early. It now uses `attempts_made < max_attempts`. This fixed the retry failures in the pipeline tests.
- **`events.py`:** `_prefix_matches` had the arguments reversed (`prefix.startswith(topic + ".")`). It now checks `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`.
- **`statemachine.py`:** `batch_order_ok` required priorities to be non-decreasing, but its docstring says non-increasing. It now returns `current_priority <= prev_priority`. It was never rejecting a dispatch, because the queue was ordering badly in the same way.
- **`config.py`:** `deep_merge` recursed with the base and override swapped, so defaults overrode per-task settings. It now recurses with the base first.
- **`scheduler.py`:** `_cascade_skip` used `dag.dependents`, which returns only direct children. It now uses `transitive_dependents`, so a permanent failure skips everything downstream.
- **`resources.py`:** `ResourcePool.release` always did `used -= 1` instead of subtracting `cost`. Pools never fully freed, so resource-limited pipelines stalled. It now does `used -= cost`.

I only checked the code against the failing tests. I didn't audit the other modules (`history.py`, `stats.py` and so on) for further bugs the suite doesn't exercise.
